description: Source repairs a historical revision needs before any fixed harness can drive it. A repair is admissible only when it is a verbatim cherry-pick of paths from a later commit that exposes machinery the target revision already contains, so the measured work stays the target revision's own. The freezer copies the entries matching a run's selected commits into the frozen config; the runner re-derives each diff from Git at apply time rather than trusting stored bytes.
rules: cherry_pick.from_commit's first parent must resolve to the repaired commit, so a repair can only ever come from the immediately following commit.
No cherry_pick path may start with 'bench/'. That directory is the harness overlay's territory, and allowing it here would let a repair smuggle harness changes into an engine revision.
The repaired revision's workload checksums must match the rest of the series exactly, which is what demonstrates the repair changed reachability rather than behaviour.

repairs.subject: Add rustia conformance base
repairs.why_it_could_not_be_measured: The root Cargo.toml predates bench/, so the overlaid harness crate was undeclared; and this revision has no public Vm::call_function, the entry point a fixed harness needs to call a workload's returned function. That entry point was added by the very next commit (aee7749), the commit that introduced the harness.
changes_applied: Added "bench" to the root Cargo.toml workspace members.
repairs.why_the_timing_is_still_this_revision: The wrapper reads settings.initial_fuel, calls call_value, and returns first_result_or_nil. All three already exist at this revision with matching signatures, so the wrapper exposes existing machinery and adds no behaviour.
repairs.why_it_is_derived_rather_than_stored: Both changes are exactly the non-bench hunks of aee7749: `git diff aee7749^ aee7749 -- Cargo.toml crates/rustia-vm/src/vm.rs` is precisely the workspace member line plus the eleven-line wrapper, and nothing else. Deriving the patch from Git makes "taken verbatim from the commit that introduced it" true by construction instead of an assertion a reviewer has to check against stored bytes.
repairs.verification: All five workload checksums match the other 74 revisions exactly.
